capabilities: Dictate notes in real time with spoken commands for headings, lists, tables, and formatting
Transcribe existing audio files or embedded recordings into notes, with optional speaker labels
Correct spelling, punctuation, and misheard terms automatically using custom and vault vocabulary
Watch a vault folder for new audio recordings and offer or run transcription automatically
Read selected text or paragraphs aloud using text-to-speech voices
extras: Several features are marked experimental (mid-sentence punctuation, listen back text-to-speech, dual-delay mode, local server mode, which needs a ~16 GB GPU). The Mistral API key is free to create; audio and vocabulary terms are sent to Mistral's cloud unless a custom base URL is used. The author accepts donations via Buy Me a Coffee.
motivation: The author built it for people who think out loud (researchers, consultants) whose best ideas arrive mid-sentence, so talk, typing, and structuring happen in one flow.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in speech-to-text, and typical dictation tools leave users a wall of unstructured text to clean up and format afterwards.

relations.evidence: A transcript is raw thinking; Parallax turns it into structured research.
the plugin's file transcription is a natural intake for Quadro's Data/ folder
It runs on Mistral's Voxtral, a speech model built for transcription from the ground up

requires.name: local vLLM server (for experimental local server mode)

summary: Dictation plugin that transcribes speech live into notes via Mistral's Voxtral, adds structure by voice, and transcribes existing audio files.
